summary: Revise at 6.4 (round 1: 5.8; Caiman 7; ship bar 7.5; for scale, Corvus was cut at 6.6 and Kraken at 7.0). Every gate is green in the JSON this round, and I checked each one against report.json and template-verification.json. The template gate now passes on the current design: 2,666,540 of 3,000,000 bytes, 1 patch, and 1,497,474 triangles, the same count as the export. The draft clamp is recorded as not applied, with a 0 mm bite. The ray release is recorded at 0.100 and 0.075 mm. It reads NotApplicable under LostWax, with 1,007 and 1,632 two-part obstructions and 1 unresolved ray at 0.075. As with the lost-wax rings that shipped (Kraken, Manticora), I treat those counts as reported numbers, not gates. The art moved, but not far enough. Beads now cover most of the face and the tail lies on the crest with rings, and the stone sits about 1.5 mm off the snout. Three problems remain. (1) The ring still does not read as a Gila monster at 300 px. In face-300 the figure is a knobbly chain of sausages with a round bulb for a head. In side.png the head is a long, pointed, crocodile-like snout with a ball eye standing proud. No light and dark bands show on the trunk. The tail rings are thin creases, not bands. (2) The face ground is cut into rectangular bead blocks with stair-stepped, pixel-quantised edges. A bald polished halo 2 to 4 mm wide surrounds the figure and the collet. Round 1 asked for a moat of 0.6 to 0.8 mm. The result reads as a masked texture decal, not as skin. (3) The shank bands still show visible seams: stepped cliffs and torn diagonal notches at band borders in palm.png (centre), radial cuts in side.png (about 7 and 8 o'clock) and a notch at the top of reverse.png, plus a polished ledge strip along both rims. One round remains, and a concrete round can close most of this.
strengths: Every gate is green and recorded in both the draft (768x320, 651,770 tris) and export (1536x448, 1,497,474 tris) blocks. The two round-1 gate punches (1 and 2) are closed: the template gate is re-run on the current design, under budget, and its triangle count matches the export.

The figure is still the collection's most distinctive silhouette. It is a full-round lizard draped over the crown, with its legs gripping the shoulders (side.png, contact-300). Nothing in Reptilia or the other Cataphracta concepts looks like it.
The tail is now on the face. It is fat, lies along the crest and carries ring segments (face.png, left). This closes most of round-1 punch 4's tail half.
The stone is tied to the animal. The collet sits about 1.5 mm off the snout (face.png, stones.png), not stranded on bare metal as it was in round 1.
The bald crown is mostly gone. A fine bead ground (0.08 mm beads at 0.46 mm pitch, per land_widths.hide) now covers the shoulders and most of the face, so density is up noticeably from round 1.

Claw tips are now measured per feature: limbs 1.57 mm, toes 0.82 mm, claw ends 0.50 mm, neck 1.44 mm and tail end 1.13 mm. This closes round-1 punch 8 on paper, and the needle tips seen in shoulder.png in round 1 are now blunt.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Better than round 1, but the ring is still three treatments. (1) The figure. (2) A face ground broken into rectangular bead blocks with bald polished gaps 2-4 mm wide around the figure and a bald oval around the collet (hero.png, face.png, reverse.png). (3) The shank's transverse coarse and fine bead bands, which meet the face ground at a visible border (reverse.png top, hero.png right edge ledges). A polished rim strip runs along both edges of the palm (palm.png) instead of the hide running to the edge fillet as the concept says.

checklist.item: The hide reads as this specific animal at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: hero-300 reads as 'a lizard on a ring'. face-300 reads as a knobbly caterpillar or a chain of sausages ending in a round bulb. The Gila head is broad, blunt and flat; here the head is a round bulb from above and a long pointed snout in profile (side.png), which reads as a crocodile or monitor. No black-and-salmon banding reads on the trunk at 300 px: the dorsal osteoderm pebbling is uniform, and the tail 'rings' are thin grooves. The shank bands read as generic granulation bands. A jeweller names a lizard, not a Gila monster.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: The figure's outline is crisp. The bead-field mask on the face is stair-stepped: the bead blocks under and beside the figure end in square-cornered steps about 1 mm on a side (hero.png lower centre, face.png above and below the trunk, stones.png). In the shank bands, some borders are stepped cliffs, and there are torn diagonal notches (palm.png centre, about x 560-650), radial cut lines (side.png, about 7 and 8 o'clock) and a notch in the band at reverse.png top centre.

checklist.item: Stones, where the ring carries one, sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: There is 1 spessartite in a made collet with a 0.52 mm wall, clearly visible in hero, face, stones.png and hero-300, with 1 reported and 1 previewed. It is still a plain bezel ringed by bald polish; it has no beaded lip tying it to the beadwork (round-1 punch 7, second half, not done).

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: The figure is sculpted. The face ground is not: rectangular bead blocks separated by polished channels read as a mechanical mask. On the shank, the bands are separated by straight ledge walls with a polished step (side.png right half, hero.png right edge), which reads as stacked strips, not as skin wrapping a form.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Not applicable. The body is a procedural HalfRound with no factory stock (bare-vs-finished.png).

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Cataphracta rings and from the Reptilia tiles
checklist.reason: The lizard figure draped over the crown (side.png, contact-300) is unlike every Reptilia tile and every other Cataphracta concept.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The large form (figure), medium forms (limbs, head, tail, collet) and small forms (beads) are present, and density is up from round 1. Legibility is below Caiman's: at 300 px the figure's surface is uniform pebble noise with no banding hierarchy, the face ground is patchy (blocks and bald gaps), and about 15-20% of the visible face is still bald polish.

gates.verified: draft 768x320: watertight true, boundary 0, non-manifold 0, degenerate 0 (651,770 tris). export 1536x448: the same (1,497,474 tris).

gates.gate: 0 self-crossings on the ring and every made part
gates.verified: geometry.self_crossings 0; made.figure_self_crossings 0; pattern.self_crossings 0; parts_joined 1; parts_notes [] at draft and export.
vertices_inside 0 at draft and export. The closest vertex is at 9.29891 mm against a 9.3 mm bore radius, which is on the bore surface.

field.process LostWax, verdict Castable (not 'with care'), thinnest wall 2.109 mm at theta 268.6, draft and export. The two-part undercut (2.01%, worst -35.7 deg; stored mesh 83.8 mm² at -90 deg) is reported, not gated, as the process allows.

Recorded in both blocks. Export 0.100: 1,007 obstructions, 0 unresolved. Export 0.075: 1,632 obstructions, 1 unresolved. Draft: 933/0 and 1,509/1. Status NotApplicable under LostWax, gated false. These are two-part pull counts, like the undercut, and the shipped lost-wax calibration rings (Kraken, Manticora) were not gated on release. I accept this as reported, not gating. The counts do mean this pattern cannot move to sand.

gates.gate: Every draft-clamp bite at most 0.05 mm
gates.verified: draft_clamp.applied false, max_bite_mm 0.0 in both blocks (min_draft 0 under lost wax).
report.json cold_reload_identical true; template-verification cold_design_reload, cold_graph_reload, source_identical and vertices_faces_normals_identical all true.
pattern watertight true, 0 degenerate, 0 self-crossings, 1,497,474 triangles.

gates.gate: Template gate: at most 4 design.set patches within the class budget
gates.verified: template_gate_passed true, class painted, template_bytes 2,666,540 <= 3,000,000, size_review_required false, 1 patch (/manufacturing), triangles 1,497,474 = the export's. Note: editable_design_bytes is 3,236,522, over 3 MB; the gated template figure is under budget.

gates.gate: Land widths (the author's own gate: 'at the floor or named')
gates.verified: The per-feature check now exists (limbs 1.57, toes 0.82, neck 1.44, tail end 1.13 mm; claw ends 0.50 mm against a self-set 0.5 mm floor). The whole-part ray read (0.00016 mm, 77.9 mm² under the floor) and the collet (0.178 mm, 26.2 mm²) pass by naming. Not a review.md gate; the 0.5 mm claw floor is a bench risk to watch.

punch_list.zone: Figure head, stone end of the Gila mesh (from the neck crease to the snout, next to the collet)
punch_list.change: Rebuild the head as a Gila wedge. The skull length should be at most 1.3x the head width. The snout should be blunt and square-ended (tip radius at least 40% of head width), not pointed. The head should be flat on top (dorsal profile within 10 deg of the neck line) and as wide as the neck or wider, with a 0.3 mm neck crease. Sink the eyes into sockets on the sides of the head so each ball is at most 0.25 mm proud of its lid; today they stand up like pins (side.png). Cover the head with the same coarse osteoderm beads as the pale bands, 0.9-1.1 mm.
punch_list.acceptance: In side.png the snout reads as blunt and rounded-square, not a crocodilian taper. In face-300 the head is a flat wedge wider than the neck, not a round bulb, and no eye ball breaks the head's outline.

punch_list.zone: Figure dorsal surface, nape to tail tip
punch_list.change: Make the banding read in metal. Alternate pale bands (domed beads 0.9-1.1 mm, at full height) with dark bands sunk 0.30-0.40 mm below the pale envelope and filled with fine beads 0.35-0.45 mm. Put 4 dark bands on the trunk and 4 on the tail, each 1.5-2.0 mm wide with forked, irregular edges. Replace the thin tail creases with these bands. Keep the pebbling uniform only within a band.
punch_list.acceptance: In face-300 a viewer can count at least 3 light/dark stripes on the trunk and 4 on the tail, and the stripe contrast is visible without zooming.

punch_list.zone: Face ground, theta about 40-140 around the figure and collet (the Gila beadwork layer that paints the face blocks)
punch_list.change: Remove the rectangular bead blocks and the bald halo. Author the face mask as smooth vector paths, or blur it by at least 1.0 mm so no edge steps. Run the fine ground continuously right up to the figure and the collet, leaving a polished moat only 0.6-0.8 mm wide following each outline. Close the bald oval around the collet the same way.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero.png, face.png, stones.png and reverse.png no bead field ends in a square corner or a step, and outside the 0.8 mm moats no polished patch wider than 1.0 mm remains on the face.

punch_list.zone: Shank bands, all eight Gila beadwork layers (theta about 150-30 through 270), band borders and tile joins
punch_list.change: Close the seams. Overlap adjacent layers by at least one coarse-bead pitch (0.8 mm) with a soft SmoothMax crossfade (soft 0.2 mm or more) so that no vertical cliff stands between bands. Make the tiling period divide the circumference (78.54 mm) exactly, which removes the radial cuts. Fix the torn diagonal notch at the palm centre and the notch at reverse.png top centre.
punch_list.acceptance: At full size in palm.png, side.png and reverse.png no continuous line crosses the band at any theta, and no band border shows a stepped wall or a torn notch.

punch_list.zone: Both rim edges of the shank (the edge fillet, theta about 150-30 through 270) and the hero's right edge ledges
punch_list.change: Carry the hide over the edge fillet as the concept specifies ('the beadwork runs to the edge fillet'). Remove the polished ledge strip and the stacked horizontal steps at the band edge; grade bead height to 0 over the last 0.4 mm into the fillet.
punch_list.acceptance: In palm.png and hero.png the hide meets the rim without a flat polished strip or a terrace of parallel lines.

punch_list.zone: Spessartite collet (at the snout, on the crest)
punch_list.change: Give the collet a milgrain or beaded lip of 0.35-0.45 mm beads, 20-26 around, so it belongs to the beadwork. Set the snout 0.6-1.0 mm from the lip rather than the present gap of about 1.5 mm.
punch_list.acceptance: In stones.png the lip reads as a bead ring. In hero-300 the stone reads as held at the animal's snout, not as a separate dot.

punch_list.zone: Tail tip (the figure's rear end, which drops off the crest in side.png at about 10 o'clock)
punch_list.change: Curl the last 4-6 mm of the tail back onto the face so the rounded tip ends on the crest and does not hang over the shoulder.
punch_list.acceptance: In side.png the tail tip stays above the shoulder line, and in face.png the tail's full length and blunt tip are visible.
